description: We are two high school students from Antalya, Türkiye, studying cybersecurity. We continuously develop software and technical skills, turning what we learn into projects that address real-world challenges. Interested in remote sensing, Earth observation, and innovative technologies, we are motivated by wildfires affecting our region to explore how satellite data can improve fire monitoring and preparedness. This project harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS hotspot data to analyze historical fire activity.
summary: ModiiZation puts NASA FIRMS MODIS Aqua and VIIRS Suomi-NPP active-fire detections for the Antalya region (2012–2025) on a common footing. We cleaned both archives without altering the raw data, flagged zero-FRP records and suspected persistent heat sources instead of deleting them, and built local-time weekly series. A robust seasonal anomaly method (log-transformed counts, median/MAD reference from the same season in other years, threshold 3.5) finds unusual fire weeks for each sensor. MODIS flagged 15 anomaly weeks and VIIRS 7, with 6 shared, including the 2021 fire period, so sensor choice changes which historical events look exceptional. We then applied a harmonization step to make the two records comparable and delivered the results in an interactive web app (built with Vercel) with a fire calendar and MODIS, VIIRS and harmonized views. ModiiZation does not forecast fires. It makes long-term records comparable so communities and fire managers can judge whether a season is truly unusual.
details:
What it does. ModiiZation puts two NASA fire records, MODIS Aqua (1 km) and VIIRS Suomi-NPP (375 m), on one comparable footing for Antalya, Türkiye (29–32.5°E, 36–37.5°N), 2012–2025. We take NASA FIRMS Standard Processing detections, keep vegetation-fire records (type 0: 9,078 VIIRS and 1,478 MODIS), and convert them into a weekly record in local time (724 weeks). For each sensor, every week is compared only with the same season in other years, using log-transformed counts and a robust median/MAD score. A score of 3.5 or more marks an anomaly week, and a floor requires at least three detections so near-empty weeks cannot create false alarms. We then compare which weeks each sensor flags: MODIS flagged 15, VIIRS 7, and 6 were flagged by both, including late July and early August 2021. In both sensors 2021 is the extreme year (about 46% of VIIRS and 55% of MODIS detections), so the choice of sensor changes which events look exceptional. This is the core of the harmonization challenge: the sensors must be made comparable before history can be read from them. The results are available in an interactive fire calendar web app, with MODIS, VIIRS and harmonized views and CSV download.

Benefits and intended impact. Fire services, forest managers and researchers get context on how unusual a season is against 14 years of history, and a documented, reproducible way to bridge the MODIS and VIIRS records. ModiiZation reads the past. It does not forecast fires or replace operational alerts. The pipeline is controlled by a bounding box, so it can be repeated for other Mediterranean regions.

Tools. Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, matplotlib, folium) in Google Colab on Mac laptops; NASA FIRMS data; the web app is deployed on Vercel. We used Claude (Anthropic) as an AI assistant for code and app development and for writing support. All analysis choices and results were reviewed by the team.

What is creative. We did not just count hot spots. We use a seasonal, robust anomaly score for each sensor, and we measure agreement between the sensors instead of assuming they match. Questionable records are flagged, not deleted, and raw files are never modified, so every step can be audited.

Factors we considered. Different pixel sizes and detection sensitivity; Aqua’s median daytime overpass drifting later (about 11:00 to 12:08 UTC, 2012 to 2025) while VIIRS stayed near 10:55; MODIS processing versions (6.03 until 2022, 61.03 from 2023); candidate persistent heat sources (about 1 km cells seen in 8 or more years) flagged rather than removed; the 2021 mega-fire year dominating the record; and local time (UTC+3) so night passes fall on the right day. We checked sensitivity across 72 parameter combinations. Limits: MODIS Aqua is sparse in this area (61% of weeks have no detection), we use Standard Processing rather than near-real-time data, and our coverage is Antalya, not all of the Mediterranean.
